cards.title: Build liquid glass from a rounded lens field
cards.decision: Map DOM rectangles into the drawing buffer, bend the procedural background at each rounded edge, and keep text in native controls above the shader.
cards.cost: This scene refracts its own generated background, not arbitrary HTML beneath it.
cards.check: Resize, switch all three finishes, move daylight, and inspect readable controls at phone size.

cards.title: Construct an orbital planet with coherent light
cards.decision: Solve the sphere hit first; layer terrain, sun-facing light, cloud shadows and a separate ring plane around the same geometry.
cards.cost: Procedural detail and atmosphere are artistic approximations rather than a planetary simulation.
cards.check: Turn the sun and verify the terminator, night lights, cloud depth and ring occlusion remain consistent.

cards.title: Shape liquid metal with a warped distance field
cards.decision: March a twisted torus with bounded steps, derive its normal from the same field, then reflect a controlled studio environment.
cards.cost: It is a deforming implicit surface, not a fluid solver or measured metal material.
cards.check: Inspect silhouette and reflections over a full motion cycle and at both control extremes.

cards.title: Give a spectral crystal a visible interior
cards.decision: Combine entry normals, a bounded interior path, thickness attenuation and restrained channel separation.
cards.cost: The stylized interior march does not solve every refracted path or total internal reflection.
cards.check: Compare thin edges with the thick center, and distinguish a missed exit from a legitimate dark region.

cards.title: Project a spatial node network onto Canvas
cards.decision: Create a fixed lattice and neighbor edges, rotate and project once per node, depth-sort, then move a signal along projected edges.
cards.cost: The sample is a decorative lattice; real network data needs a truthful graph model and labels.
cards.check: Change connectivity and send a signal without losing depth or creating a new graph every frame.

cards.title: Build a kinetic tunnel from radial depth
cards.decision: Convert a polygonal radial field to bounded depth, then use repeating phase for rings and angle for light rails.
cards.cost: The perspective impression is screen-space and high-speed contrast can be uncomfortable.
cards.check: Keep the center finite and make reduced motion retain a complete static scene.

cards.title: Build an editorial spread with a reading layer
cards.decision: Pair a restrained text column with an authored SVG, then open long-form content in a native reading dialog.
cards.cost: The composition needs real story hierarchy and a deliberate phone crop, not just a serif font.
cards.check: Read long paragraphs at narrow width and close the story back to its trigger.

cards.title: Keep an energy dashboard and its totals synchronized
cards.decision: Drive the chart, total and peak from one selected interval series and derive all summaries from it.
cards.cost: Illustrative battery and device state are not live telemetry or backend controls.
cards.check: Switch periods and independently sum the displayed buckets; label units and sample data.

cards.title: Connect a product configurator to a live material preview
cards.decision: Use one selected finish and light level to update SVG materials, labels and the review summary.
cards.cost: A selection preview does not implement a cart, payment or real pricing authority.
cards.check: Change each option with keyboard and confirm the summary reflects the current state.

cards.title: Give a timeline workspace one transport clock
cards.decision: Derive active clip, playhead, time label and SVG preview from one bounded sequence position.
cards.cost: The demo previews four vector scenes; it is not a media encoder or a nonlinear video engine.
cards.check: Seek across each clip boundary, pause, resume and reach the exact sequence end.

cards.title: Draw a contour landscape from a bounded height field
cards.decision: Sample layered curves from one sine-and-Gaussian field; let relief change amplitude while depth controls spacing.
cards.cost: A Canvas contour impression does not provide a 3D terrain mesh or physical topography.
cards.check: Compare zero relief, both slider endpoints, pause and resize without non-finite coordinates.

cards.title: Give GPU simulation an explicit previous and next state
cards.decision: Lay out host and shader bytes together, alternate read/write storage buffers, and advance fixed simulation steps before rendering.
cards.cost: Device loss invalidates all resources; mapping results to the CPU each frame can erase the compute benefit.
cards.check: Dispatch a non-multiple of the workgroup size, pause, resize and rebuild after resource loss.

cards.title: Turn audio transients into controlled visual energy
cards.decision: Smooth a normalized feature with separate attack and release constants, then map the bounded envelope to one visual parameter.
cards.cost: Raw frequency bins and frame-dependent smoothing produce noisy or device-dependent motion.
cards.check: Compare the same signal at two frame rates and verify silence returns to the idle composition.

cards.title: Implement interruptible motion with a single property owner
cards.decision: Select a state transition, reorder or scroll pattern; define its interrupt and reduced-motion state before adding choreography.
cards.cost: Multiple timelines writing the same transform can make state and presentation disagree.
cards.check: Reverse input mid-transition, resize, and navigate away before completion.

cards.title: Keep stale requests from replacing current results
cards.decision: Derive local values during render; give async work cancellation or identity tied to the current query and screen.
cards.cost: Moving everything into client effects can lose initial content and duplicate server work.
cards.check: Resolve two queries in reverse order and navigate away while the slower request is pending.

cards.title: Preserve selection when a native interface changes panes
cards.decision: Store selection and navigation with their durable owner; derive compact or expanded presentation from current constraints.
cards.cost: A recreated view may lose draft content or run duplicate lifecycle work if it owns persistent state.
cards.check: Resize, return from background and scale text without losing selection or making controls unreachable.

cards.title: Share one command path across desktop controls
cards.decision: Let menus, shortcuts and toolbars invoke the same command; separate document state from reusable cells and disposable views.
cards.cost: Independent click handlers can bypass validation, dirty-state or undo semantics.
cards.check: Invoke through keyboard and toolbar, recycle a cell, cancel background work and launch the packaged artifact.

cards.title: Make the offer readable at first contact
cards.decision: Place the product, intended customer, and next action in one readable opening group. Let imagery explain a concrete attribute of the offer.
cards.cost: A short opening cannot carry every exception; place the important conditions where the decision is made.
cards.check: Read the opening without animation and identify what is offered and what the action does.

cards.title: Put evidence beside the question it answers
cards.decision: Attach real measurements, examples, or conditions to the claim they support. Keep the evidence interpretable without leaving the decision.
cards.cost: Large proof sections can interrupt reading; choose the evidence that changes the decision.
cards.check: Confirm the source, date, unit, and scope of each factual claim used.

cards.title: Shape the screen around the next item of work
cards.decision: Show actionable items with enough context to choose the next one. Keep the selection and its available actions close together.
cards.cost: A worklist emphasizes repeated tasks and may need a separate view for aggregate analysis.
cards.check: Complete one item, recover from one failure, and verify that the next item remains easy to find.

cards.title: Preserve the identity of a dense table row
cards.decision: Keep the identifier and decisive fields visible while less frequent attributes can be revealed. Align comparable values and preserve selection through sorting.
cards.cost: Hiding columns saves width but can obscure comparisons; expose a deliberate way to recover them.
cards.check: Inspect a long identifier, missing values, sorting, and keyboard movement at narrow width.

cards.title: Choose the encoding from the analytical question
cards.decision: Name the relationship being examined, then choose the simplest encoding that makes that relationship visible.
cards.cost: An expressive visualization can make exact value lookup harder; keep the necessary values available.
cards.check: Ask a reader to answer the intended question using the shown units and time range.

cards.title: Separate an absent measurement from a zero
cards.decision: Represent unavailable, loading, stale, and zero values as distinct states when their meaning differs.
cards.cost: More states require concise labels; avoid making every cell an explanatory paragraph.
cards.check: Render each actual data state and verify that none implies a fabricated measurement.

cards.title: Give long reading a stable route back
cards.decision: Use meaningful headings, a comfortable reading measure, and navigation suited to the document's length.
cards.cost: Persistent navigation consumes width and may need to become an explicit control on a phone.
cards.check: Enter through a deep link, read a long section, and find the neighboring topic.

cards.title: Design against the longest credible content
cards.decision: Test realistic long labels and titles before settling component heights or breakpoints. Let wrapping preserve meaning.
cards.cost: Variable height affects alignment; decide which comparisons need a shared baseline.
cards.check: Inspect long content with text scaling and without relying on a tooltip to reveal essential information.

cards.title: Choose type using a sample of actual roles
cards.decision: Compare title, paragraph, label, and numeric samples in the actual language. Establish a small hierarchy before adding another face.
cards.cost: A distinctive display face can need a quieter companion for dense content.
cards.check: Inspect fallback fonts, loaded weights, punctuation, and aligned numbers.

cards.title: Assign the strongest accent a specific job
cards.decision: Reserve the strongest color relationship for the priority action or information. Give feedback states their own comprehensible treatment.
cards.cost: Accent restraint may require scale or placement to establish secondary hierarchy.
cards.check: Inspect the screen in each supported theme and verify status remains understandable without color.

cards.title: Label an ambiguous icon action
cards.decision: Use an action label when a symbol is not unambiguous in this product. Keep neighboring icons optically consistent.
cards.cost: Labels consume room; reduce low-priority actions before removing essential meaning.
cards.check: Identify each action without hovering and confirm the accessible name matches its effect.

cards.title: Rebuild the phone order around the task
cards.decision: Place current context and the next action in a coherent phone sequence instead of preserving desktop column order automatically.
cards.cost: Different visual and document orders can confuse navigation; keep the semantic sequence intentional.
cards.check: Complete the primary path at phone width with the keyboard open when inputs are involved.

cards.title: Use additional space to reveal a related pane
cards.decision: Keep selection stable while moving between a single-pane and a related multi-pane view.
cards.cost: More visible context raises density; each pane still needs a clear role.
cards.check: Resize during an active selection and verify state, focus, and content continuity.

cards.title: Keep keyboard context through a modal
cards.decision: Choose the initial focus, keep interaction within the modal boundary, and return focus to a useful place after dismissal.
cards.cost: The original trigger may disappear; define a sensible return target for that actual case.
cards.check: Open, traverse, dismiss, and reopen the dialog entirely by keyboard.

cards.title: Make a failed form preserve useful work
cards.decision: Keep valid values, identify the fields that need attention, and explain what changed after a failed submission.
cards.cost: Some sensitive fields cannot be retained; explain the real requirement where it matters.
cards.check: Submit invalid data, repair one field, retry, and inspect focus and repeated messages.

cards.title: Match confirmation to real recovery
cards.decision: Use an undo path when the operation is genuinely reversible; use an explicit confirmation when the consequence needs a decision beforehand.
cards.cost: An undo promise creates persistence and timing obligations.
cards.check: Perform the action and its advertised recovery on representative data.

cards.title: Acknowledge input while the result is pending
cards.decision: Show that input was received immediately, then communicate the result when it is known. Keep duplicate activation behavior deliberate.
cards.cost: Multiple feedback channels can become noisy; give each phase one clear signal.
cards.check: Try a slow response, a failure, and rapid repeated activation.

cards.title: Make an animation survive a change of mind
cards.decision: Define how motion settles when another action arrives before completion. Keep the underlying state authoritative.
cards.cost: Interruptible motion may need a simpler transition than a fixed cinematic sequence.
cards.check: Reverse, repeat, and navigate away during the animation.

cards.title: Preserve the message when travel is removed
cards.decision: Replace the movement with a readable state change while keeping the same information and controls available.
cards.cost: Some sequences need a separately composed static arrangement.
cards.check: Enable reduced motion and complete the same task without waiting on the removed animation.

cards.title: Let each scroll segment reveal useful information
cards.decision: Connect the scroll distance to a readable content progression and retain ordinary navigation.
cards.cost: Long pinned sequences delay access to later content.
cards.check: Use keyboard navigation, a short viewport, and the static or reduced-motion view.

cards.title: Make the object identifiable before adding surface detail
cards.decision: Build the structural features the intended camera must read before spending detail on a material.
cards.cost: Silhouette detail may require geometry that cannot be replaced by a texture.
cards.check: Inspect an untextured view at the final camera distance and identify the object.

cards.title: Tie shoreline foam to wave contact
cards.decision: Relate foam and wave behavior to shallows and obstacles, while preserving coherent movement from open water toward the coast.
cards.cost: An artistic depth or distance approximation needs tuning for the camera and shoreline.
cards.check: Watch a full wave cycle and verify that contact cues remain attached to the coast.

cards.title: Make shader coordinate spaces agree
cards.decision: Track the space and units of positions, directions, and normals through the material and lighting calculation.
cards.cost: An extra transform can be correct but expensive; optimize only after the image is correct.
cards.check: Move the camera and object independently and inspect illumination and highlights.

cards.title: Reduce the measured expensive part of the frame
cards.decision: Measure the complete frame, identify a costly pass, and reduce its unnecessary work before lowering every quality setting.
cards.cost: CPU and GPU timing tools expose different parts of latency; report the measurement boundary.
cards.check: Compare equivalent scenes, resolution, and hardware, then inspect the changed image.

cards.title: Test the scene across time and interruption
cards.decision: Give simulation steps and render frames explicit time ownership and limit catch-up after a pause.
cards.cost: A stable simulation can need interpolation or a lower update frequency.
cards.check: Pause, resume, resize, and move the camera while inspecting continuity.

cards.title: Map audio to a few legible visual roles
cards.decision: Use measured bands or envelopes with deliberate smoothing and headroom for transient peaks.
cards.cost: Too many simultaneous mappings obscure cause and effect.
cards.check: Test silence, a sustained tone, rhythmic input, and abrupt peaks.

cards.title: Judge an image inside its actual container
cards.decision: Design the focal point and negative space for the final placement, including its phone crop.
cards.cost: One source image may not support radically different aspect ratios.
cards.check: Inspect the actual crop beside its text at every required composition.

cards.title: Compose moving media for the whole loop
cards.decision: Choose a useful poster and inspect the loop join, framing, and readability over moving frames.
cards.cost: Continuous playback consumes resources and can compete with the content.
cards.check: Inspect start, middle, end, loop join, and the state before playback is available.

cards.title: Map a design component to the component that exists
cards.decision: Associate the relevant design properties and states with their actual runtime owners before implementing or exporting a mapping.
cards.cost: A visually similar component may have incompatible behavior.
cards.check: Exercise mapped variants and compare the implementation at the reference dimensions.

cards.title: Let the owning view release its resources
cards.decision: Tie subscriptions, animation, and background work to the view or application state that owns them.
cards.cost: Shared resources need ownership broader than a single screen.
cards.check: Enter and leave the view repeatedly and observe pending work and retained resources.

cards.title: Keep desktop work out of the interaction thread
cards.decision: Run expensive work away from the UI thread, then apply results through the framework's UI update mechanism.
cards.cost: Cancellation and a disappearing view require explicit result ownership.
cards.check: Interact and resize while the work runs, then close the owning view.

cards.title: Attach a critique to an observed consequence
cards.decision: Point to the element or state causing confusion and describe how it affects reading or action before proposing a change.
cards.cost: A static capture cannot expose every interaction failure.
cards.check: Reproduce the relevant state and distinguish the defect from an optional stylistic alternative.

react.inspect: Component state ownership and the rendered DOM.
react.decide: Keep the state driving an interaction with its actual owner.
react.check: Exercise rerenders, focus, and an asynchronous update.

nextjs.inspect: Existing server/client boundaries and route behavior.
nextjs.decide: Give client behavior to the interactive part that needs it.
nextjs.check: Inspect initial rendering, hydration, and route transitions.

vue.inspect: Reactive state, component bindings, and slots.
vue.decide: Follow the component's actual data flow when presenting state.
vue.check: Change the bound data and inspect the resulting DOM and focus.

svelte.inspect: Version-specific state conventions and element ownership.
svelte.decide: Use framework-owned updates for elements managed by the framework.
svelte.check: Exercise state changes while a transition is active.

astro.inspect: Static content and existing interactive islands.
astro.decide: Hydrate only the surface whose behavior requires it.
astro.check: Read and navigate before interaction code is ready.

nuxtjs.inspect: Routes, server data, and shared reactive state.
nuxtjs.decide: Retain useful content while refreshing route data.
nuxtjs.check: Navigate between populated and empty states.

nuxt-ui.inspect: Installed component APIs and theme configuration.
nuxt-ui.decide: Express design changes through supported variants and local slots.
nuxt-ui.check: Inspect generated semantics and keyboard behavior.

angular.inspect: Form ownership, change detection, and shared components.
angular.decide: Connect visible validation to the application's existing form state.
angular.check: Submit, repair, and resubmit without losing valid input.

laravel.inspect: Templates, server validation, and authorization boundaries.
laravel.decide: Keep entered values and actionable errors after a failed request.
laravel.check: Exercise the form with real server validation.

swiftui.inspect: View identity, observable state, and navigation.
swiftui.decide: Let stable application state survive view reconstruction.
swiftui.check: Try Dynamic Type, navigation return, and lifecycle changes.

react-native.inspect: Native input behavior, list rendering, and screen lifecycle.
react-native.decide: Keep keyboard and touch paths responsive under realistic data.
react-native.check: Open the keyboard, scroll a populated list, and return to the screen.

flutter.inspect: Widget constraints, identity, and controller ownership.
flutter.decide: Model responsive relationships within actual layout constraints.
flutter.check: Scale text, resize, and dispose the owning screen.

jetpack-compose.inspect: State hoisting, semantics, and lifecycle-aware work.
jetpack-compose.decide: Keep UI state and background results connected to the correct owner.
jetpack-compose.check: Inspect recomposition behavior and restored screen state.

html-tailwind.inspect: Document order, local tokens, and installed utilities.
html-tailwind.decide: Use semantic elements and derive layout from content relationships.
html-tailwind.check: Verify focus, long text, and intermediate viewport widths.

shadcn.inspect: The project's actual copied component implementations.
shadcn.decide: Change shared behavior where that component owns it.
shadcn.check: Exercise the edited component's visible and keyboard states.

threejs.inspect: Camera, render loop, resource lifetime, and material conventions.
threejs.decide: Establish recognizable geometry and lighting before extra passes.
threejs.check: Inspect movement, resizing, exposure, and resource cleanup.

javafx.inspect: Scene graph layout, observable properties, and UI-thread work.
javafx.decide: Keep long work cancellable and owned by the appropriate view.
javafx.check: Resize under load and inspect reused cells and keyboard navigation.

wpf.inspect: Bindings, commands, dispatcher work, and data collection size.
wpf.decide: Connect UI state to the established binding and command model.
wpf.check: Inspect DPI changes, keyboard use, and a large collection.

winui.inspect: Window model, adaptive panes, and focus navigation.
winui.decide: Preserve selection while adapting the relationship between panes.
winui.check: Resize the window and inspect focus and scaling.

avalonia.inspect: Target platforms, resource lookup, bindings, and input conventions.
avalonia.decide: Keep shared intent while respecting each target's behavior.
avalonia.check: Exercise the relevant platform rather than relying only on compilation.

uno.inspect: Target platform differences and the shared view model.
uno.decide: Keep responsive behavior compatible with the actual target controls.
uno.check: Run the affected screen on the intended platform.

uwp.inspect: Application lifecycle, adaptive layout, and focus behavior.
uwp.decide: Preserve meaningful screen state through lifecycle changes.
uwp.check: Inspect scaling, keyboard use, and resumed state.
